raw_text:
# 4-Week Postpartum On-Ramp Programme

**Client snapshot:** 10 weeks postpartum, OB-cleared for moderate exercise, no jumping for 4 more weeks. Training at home with light dumbbells.

## Programming Principles for This Block

- **Rebuild the inner unit first.** Breath mechanics, transverse abdominis, pelvic floor, and glutes are the foundation. We don't load over a leaking system.
- **No jumping, no high-impact, no max breath-holds (no Valsalva), no traditional crunches/sit-ups/planks-on-toes in Weeks 1–2.** Reintroduce planks late in the block only if she's symptom-free.
- **Watch for red flags every session:** doming/coning at the linea alba, pelvic heaviness, urinary leaking, lower back or pubic symphysis pain, or bleeding returning. Any of these = regress immediately and consider pelvic floor PT referral.
- **Cue exhale on exertion** throughout. Inhale on the easy part, exhale on the lift/press/effort, with a gentle pelvic floor lift on the exhale.
- **Sessions are short by design.** Sleep is broken, recovery is poor, and feeding demands are high. Done > optimal.

---

## Week 1 — Acclimatisation

**Goal:** Reconnect breath, core, and pelvic floor. Get blood moving. Confirm tolerance. This is *not* a training week — it's an assessment-in-motion.

**Frequency:** 3 sessions, 20–25 minutes each. Plus daily 10–20 min walks if tolerated.

### Session A — Breath & Core Reconnection (Day 1, 4, 6 or similar)

All sessions this week use the same structure. The goal is repetition and confidence, not novelty.

**Warm-up (5 min)**
- 90/90 diaphragmatic breathing — 2 min, focus on 360° rib expansion on inhale, full exhale with gentle pelvic floor lift
- Cat-cow — 8 slow reps
- Glute bridge with exhale-and-lift — 10 reps, no weight

**Main work (12–15 min) — 2 rounds, rest as needed**
- Heel slides (supine, one leg at a time) — 8/side
- Bird dog (no weight, slow tempo) — 6/side
- Side-lying clamshell — 10/side
- Wall sit-to-stand or box squat to a chair, bodyweight — 10 reps
- Standing dumbbell shoulder press, very light (2–4 kg) — 10 reps
- Bent-over dumbbell row, light — 10/side

**Cool-down (3–5 min)**
- Child's pose, supported pigeon, supine hamstring stretch

**Notes for Week 1:** No DOMS goal. If she's sore the next day, drop a round. Watch for any doming when she stands up off the floor — that tells you a lot.

---

## Week 2 — Build the Base

**Goal:** Add a second movement pattern per session, introduce light loaded carries, extend session length slightly.

**Frequency:** 3 sessions, 25–30 minutes. Continue daily walking.

### Session A — Lower Body Focus

**Warm-up (5 min)**
- 90/90 breathing — 1 min
- Glute bridge — 12 reps
- World's greatest stretch — 4/side
- Banded or bodyweight monster walks — 10 steps each direction

**Main (3 rounds)**
- Goblet squat to box, light DB (4–8 kg) — 10 reps
- Romanian deadlift, light DBs — 10 reps
- Reverse lunge (no weight or very light) — 8/side
- Dead bug with exhale — 6/side

**Finisher**
- Suitcase carry — 20 m/side x 2 (light)

### Session B — Upper Body Focus

**Warm-up (5 min)** — breathing, cat-cow, scap CARs, band pull-aparts

**Main (3 rounds)**
- DB floor press — 10 reps
- DB single-arm row — 10/side
- Half-kneeling DB shoulder press — 8/side
- Standing Pallof press (band) or DB anti-rotation hold — 8/side

**Finisher**
- Farmer carry, light — 20 m x 2

### Session C — Full Body Flow

- Goblet squat — 8
- DB RDL — 8
- Push-up on incline (counter or wall) — 8
- DB row — 8/side
- Bird dog — 6/side
- Glute bridge — 12

3–4 rounds, rest 60–90 s between rounds.

**Check-in at end of Week 2:** Any doming? Any leaking? Bleeding? Energy levels? Adjust Week 3 load up or hold steady accordingly.

---

## Week 3 — Add Load, Add Pattern Complexity

**Goal:** Begin progressive overload on the main lifts. Introduce split stance and single-leg work. Begin gentle anti-extension/anti-rotation core.

**Frequency:** 3–4 sessions, 30–35 minutes.

### Session A — Lower Body

- Goblet squat, heavier DB (8–12 kg) — 3 x 10
- DB RDL — 3 x 10
- Split squat, rear foot on floor — 3 x 8/side
- Glute bridge with march — 2 x 8/side
- Side plank from knees — 2 x 20 s/side *(only if no doming)*

### Session B — Upper Body & Carries

- DB floor press or bench press — 3 x 10
- DB row — 3 x 10/side
- Half-kneeling press — 3 x 8/side
- DB biceps curl + triceps kickback superset — 2 x 10
- Farmer carry — 3 x 30 m

### Session C — Full Body / Conditioning Substitute

Because she can't jump, we use carries, step-ups, and tempo work for conditioning.

Circuit, 4 rounds, 30 s on / 30 s rest:
- Step-up to low box — alternating
- DB push press, light (sub for jumping)
- DB Romanian deadlift
- Suitcase carry in place (march)
- Dead bug

### Optional Session D — Mobility & Core

- Breathing drills, hip mobility flow, bird dogs, side planks (knees), Pallof press. 20 minutes.

---

## Week 4 — Establish Working Baseline

**Goal:** Confirm loads she can repeat consistently. This becomes the on-ramp from which the next block (Weeks 5–8) builds. Test tolerance for slightly higher intensity — still no jumping until cleared at the 14-week mark.

**Frequency:** 4 sessions, 35–40 minutes.

### Session A — Lower Body (heaviest day)

- Goblet squat — 4 x 8 (find a load that's RPE 7)
- DB RDL — 4 x 8
- Split squat — 3 x 10/side
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3 x 10/side
- Side plank (knees or full) — 3 x 30 s/side

### Session B — Upper Body Push/Pull

- DB bench or floor press — 4 x 8
- DB row — 4 x 8/side
- Standing DB shoulder press — 3 x 10
- DB reverse fly — 3 x 12
- Pallof press — 3 x 10/side

### Session C — Posterior Chain & Carries

- DB RDL — 4 x 8
- Hip thrust off couch/bench — 3 x 12
- DB row — 3 x 10/side
- Farmer carry — 3 x 40 m
- Suitcase carry — 3 x 20 m/side

### Session D — Full Body Flow / Movement Quality

- Goblet squat — 3 x 10
- Push-up (incline as needed) — 3 x 8
- DB row — 3 x 10/side
- Reverse lunge — 3 x 8/side
- Dead bug — 3 x 8/side
- Bird dog — 3 x 8/side

---

## Recovery & Lifestyle Notes

- **Sleep is the limiter, not training.** If she had a 2-hour stretch the night before, drop a round or skip the finisher. Don't let her chase fatigue she can't recover from.
- **Hydration:** if she's breastfeeding, fluid needs are elevated — aim 2.5–3 L/day plus electrolytes on training days.
- **Nutrition (if she asks):** maintenance or slight surplus, *not* a deficit. Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight. This is not the block to chase fat loss — strength and tissue repair come first. Revisit body composition goals in the next block if she raises them.
- **Pelvic floor:** if she has any leaking, urgency, heaviness, or unresolved diastasis (gap >2 finger-widths with poor tension) by end of Week 4 — refer to a pelvic floor physiotherapist before progressing load.

## What Comes Next (Weeks 5–8 preview)

Assuming a clean Week 4: introduce barbell or heavier DB work, hinge progressions, push-up progressions off the floor, low-impact conditioning (bike, brisk incline walks, sled if available), and — once 14-week mark passes and OB clears impact — gradual return to hopping and jumping mechanics, starting with pogo drills and double-leg low hops before anything bilateral fast.
